Thought: Controlled evaluation paper, no new method. 100 OMIM phenotype entries, each drafted by one model (Claude Opus 5.5) from exactly the cited papers. The strategies are direct long-context reading, an agentic curator, an evidence graph, case-table-first, recall-then-verify, a memory-only control, and three add-ons. The primary endpoint is coverage of fixed fact lists split once from OMIM allelic-variant text in ClinVar. Strongest evidence is the within-paper access manipulation: hiding the full text drops coverage from 79.8 to 36.1 (45/0/1 entries), an effect far too large to be a judge artefact. The 'strategies within a point' result is backed by paired bootstrap, sign tests, replicate noise (half-width 1.0) and judge variation. Statistical hygiene is unusually good: completion is treated as an outcome with a symmetric exclusion rule, an ITT sensitivity analysis is given, fact lists are fixed rather than re-split per draft, and corrected analyses are disclosed. Main concerns: (a) every judgement (fact splitting, presence, 'stated in text', audit) comes from the writer's own model family, and no human checks even a sample. That is a serious gap for a benchmark contribution, because 95.7% judge self-agreement measures consistency, not validity. (b) The headline is expected and depends on the regime: 81% of papers are abstract/title-only and inputs fit one prompt, the setting where long-context direct reading should win. Yet for full-text papers 49% of missed facts were stated in the text, so selection still matters there. The regime where strategy should matter (many relevant papers) failed because of safety-filter stops. (c) The reference is narrow: per the paper, 24% of draft statements have a counterpart. (d) The released-system comparison is small (10 and 4 entries) and handicapped: a 384-dim bge-small embedder replaces the defaults, PaperQA2 runs without its agent, QA systems are forced through 6 section questions, and the systems get no repair round. STORM failed because of the model provider, not because of STORM. (e) Presentation is extremely dense, with 47 tables and heavily hedged, number-packed prose. Significance for ICLR is modest: a domain-specific benchmark, one model, and largely confirmatory findings. The rigour is high, but the generality and validation are not enough for ICLR. Leaning reject, persuadable with human validation and a second judge family.
Summary: The paper builds a controlled benchmark for evidence-grounded knowledge-base writing from 100 OMIM phenotype entries (2-12 references each; 515 papers, 19% readable in full via open access, the rest abstract or title only). Each entry is written from its header and exactly the papers its curators cited, with the causal gene withheld. A single model (Claude Opus 5.5) writes every draft. All strategies share the same guards (ontology-candidate selection, HGNC normalisation, mandatory citation of supplied papers), a claim-level audit with one repair round, and the same scoring. The strategies are three paradigms (read-and-write: direct reading and an agentic curator; extract-then-write: an evidence graph and case-table-first; memory-first: recall-then-verify), a memory-only control, and three add-ons (second-hand evidence from citing papers, a reconciled case database, a learned curation guide). The primary endpoint is 'OMIM facts conveyed': coverage of fixed fact lists (6,652 facts over 476 paragraphs) split once, before any draft was seen, from OMIM's allelic-variant descriptions as deposited in ClinVar. Secondary measures are HPO synopsis terms, allelic variants, causal gene and inheritance.
